newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland says dismantling of Red Army monument legal.
newsitem.headline: Poland says dismantling of Red Army monument legal.

text.p: Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati said on Wednesday a Polish city's decision to dismantle a Soviet army memorial was legal but the measure lacked the tact needed when dealing with such monuments.

Russian authorities have protested about the decision of the city of Torun, northwest of Warsaw, to dismantle the monument, erected in honour of Soviet troops who died liberating Poland from the Nazis at the end of World War Two.

The news agency PAP quoted Rosati as saying the memorial had been partially dismantled but that official plaques from the structure had been moved to a nearby cemetery housing the graves of Soviet soldiers.

"In effect what we have witnessed is a change of location of the memorial, (and) of its form... (because) the plaques hold the symbolic and emotional values of the memorial," PAP quoted Rosati as telling a news conference.
Russia's ambassador to Warsaw described the city's action as unfriendly.
"We believe that this action has a clearly unfriendly character and shows a lack of understanding of how to live in good neighbourly relations," PAP quoted envoy Leonid Drakchevski as saying.

PAP said the Polish Foreign Ministry had asked Torun officials to not to destroy the monument' because of the effect such a move would have on relations with Russia at a time when Poland was seeking to join NATO but the city went ahead with its plans.
